title: Gustar, and things that hurt
vocabFocus: me gusta / gustan, doler; body parts
listenFocus: Someone describing likes and a minor ailment
practiceFocus: Describe three likes or dislikes and one ache

points.title: Gustar works backwards
points.rule: Day 9 only used me gusta with one thing or one verb. The thing you like is the subject, so a plural thing needs gustan, not gusta. The person who likes it comes first: me, te, le, nos, les. Doler, encantar, and interesar follow the same pattern.

examples.spanish: Me gusta el café. Me gustan los libros.
examples.english: One thing uses gusta. More than one uses gustan.

examples.spanish: Te gusta. Le gusta. Nos gusta. Les gusta.
examples.english: The person who likes it comes first.
His or her feet hurt. Plural, so duelen.

grammar.notYet: Gustaría, and combining gustar with the pronouns from day 17.

phrases.spanish: Me gustan los libros de historia.

phrases.english: I am interested in modern art.

phrases.note: Doler, same pattern. Body parts: la cabeza, el estómago, la garganta, la espalda, el pie, el brazo, la mano.

phrases.spanish: Nos duele la espalda después de correr.
No me gusta nada el ruido.
phrases.english: I don’t like noise at all.
I have to go to the doctor.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.english: How are you? You look tired.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Me duele un poco la cabeza. Y me duele la espalda.
lines.english: My head hurts a bit. And my back hurts.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.spanish: ¿Te gusta el té de manzanilla? Ayuda con el dolor.
lines.english: Do you like chamomile tea? It helps with the pain.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.english: Yes, I like it a lot. Do you have any?

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.spanish: Sí. A mí también me duelen los pies. Caminé mucho hoy.
lines.english: Yes. My feet hurt too. I walked a lot today.

practice.title: Likes and one ache
practice.instruction: Say three things you like or don’t like. Mix one singular thing and one plural thing, using me gusta and me gustan. Then say one thing that hurts, using me duele or me duelen.
tips: Check the noun’s number before you choose gusta or gustan.
The pattern follows the thing, not the person.
